payload.comment:
The evaluation stage is internally consistent and correctly computed. All arithmetic checks pass: confusion matrix rows sum to per-class supports (total 7,180), accuracy (6,375/7,180 = 0.887883), balanced accuracy, macro-F1, macro-precision, and macro-recall are all mutually consistent. The prediction artifact (7,180 test samples, 10,004 validation samples) matches the evaluation report. No deterministic errors were found.

However, the results reveal a severe generalization gap that warrants attention:

1. **Validation-to-test accuracy drop:** Best validation accuracy was 0.997201 (epoch 11), yet test accuracy is 0.887883 — an ~11-point decline. Validation macro-F1 was 0.997242 vs. test macro-F1 of 0.855476 (~14-point drop). This magnitude of gap suggests the validation set is not representative of the test distribution, or the model has overfit to validation-specific patterns.

2. **Per-class failure modes:** Three classes are substantially underperforming: cancer-associated stroma (F1=0.647, recall=0.508), smooth muscle (F1=0.705, recall=0.799), and debris (F1=0.727, precision=0.614). The confusion matrix shows systematic confusion: adipose→smooth muscle (178), cancer-associated stroma→debris (105) and →smooth muscle (71), smooth muscle→background (61) and →debris (42). These are morphologically similar tissue types, suggesting the model struggles with fine-grained histological distinctions.

3. **ROC AUC vs. accuracy discrepancy:** The OVR macro ROC-AUC of 0.9798 is high, indicating good ranking ability, but the decision boundary is poorly calibrated for the weaker classes, particularly at the default 0.5 threshold.

4. **Prior-stage minor issues (carried forward):** Rationale strings are truncated in multiple configs, limiting full auditability. The early_stopping_patience escalation from 1 (search) to 3 (final training) is not explicitly documented as a deliberate design choice in the rationale text.

The evaluation itself is correctly executed and the metrics are trustworthy. The generalization gap is a model-quality finding, not an evaluation error. The pipeline should consider whether the validation split is representative, whether additional regularization or data augmentation targeting the weak classes would help, and whether the selection criterion (validation accuracy) is the best proxy for test performance in this regime.
llm_issues: Severe validation-to-test generalization gap: val_acc 0.9972 → test_acc 0.8879 (~11 pt drop); val_macro_f1 0.9972 → test_macro_f1 0.8555 (~14 pt drop)
Cancer-associated stroma (class 7) severely underperforming: F1=0.647, recall=0.508; 105/421 misclassified as debris, 71 as smooth muscle
Smooth muscle (class 5) underperforming: F1=0.705, recall=0.799; 61/592 misclassified as background, 42 as debris
Debris (class 2) low precision: 0.614; 105 samples from class 7 and 42 from class 5 incorrectly assigned to debris
Adipose (class 0) recall only 0.843; 178/1338 misclassified as smooth muscle, 23 as adenocarcinoma
Rationale strings truncated in best_configuration, train_config, and trial configs (end with '…'), reducing full auditability
early_stopping_patience changed from 1 (search trials) to 3 (final training) without explicit in-rationale documentation of the deliberate escalation
Selection was based on validation accuracy (0.982707) which does not reflect test performance (0.887883), suggesting the selection criterion may be unreliable for this dataset split
